message.text: `#follow` treats a link as inside the install only if its target lies beneath the nearest chain directory that holds the link. When the module the install is read from sits inside a pnpm store (`node_modules/.pnpm/<pkg>@<v>/node_modules/<pkg>/…`), that store entry directory holds its own `node_modules`, so it becomes `chain[0]`. pnpm always installs a package's dependencies as sibling links in that `node_modules`, pointing at `../../<dep>@<v>/node_modules/<dep>`. Those targets are outside `chain[0]`, so every one is recorded as `links outside` and the install reads unidentified. This is the layout the instrumenter resolves to in any pnpm checkout, and the layout Melian's own modules sit in when Melian is installed with pnpm.

evidence.snippet:
const attaches =
			reusable &&
			known !== undefined &&
			known.lenses.join("\n") === selection.join("\n") &&
			record !== undefined &&
			(record.state.status !== "terminal" || finished(record, undecided)) &&
			!(await lensFailed(record!, refused, (id) => harness.snapshot(ProbingDocument, id, context), !rerun));

Choice: One lens task per head, and one adjudication task per head and input, recorded in a root index; a repeat call attaches, never duplicates, and an adjudication the index no longer names records no verdict

Why: A crash must not double the model spend, nor let an older verdict overwrite a newer one

A link out of the project that holds it counts as a link out of the install. Melian's round at `31c0dd74e` found that a stray `node_modules` in a home directory raised the install root to that directory, so `npm link yaml` from a checkout to `~/work/yaml` read as a link inside, keyed only its manifest, and left the install identified. A link's target now counts as inside only when it lies beneath the nearest directory of the module's chain that holds the link. Nearest to the module would not do: `packages/pipeline` holds a `node_modules` of its own, so every workspace link in the root's `node_modules` would read as outside. In a checkout, the repository root holds those links, so they stay inside, and so do a pnpm store's links between its packages. Each is a named test. Two residuals stay: a link inside the project to a directory that is no workspace package, such as npm's `file:./vendor/x`, keys only its manifest, and a link in the stray `node_modules` itself is judged against the directory that holds it.

explanation.whatToDo: Judge whether a link is inside against the install root, or against the nearest chain directory that is a project root (one holding a package.json that is no store entry), not against a pnpm store entry. Add a test that reads from a module inside `.pnpm/pi@1.1.0/node_modules/pi/dist` where `.pnpm/pi@1.1.0/node_modules/sdk` links to `../../sdk@2.0.0/node_modules/sdk`, and expect `identified: true`.
explanation.whyHere: The base decision on review attachment says a repeat call attaches and never duplicates, so that a crash does not double the model spend. The head amends that only for an install Melian cannot identify, and it says a pnpm store's links between its packages stay inside. In the code, an unidentified install sets `reusable` to false in `reviewChangeset`. `runLenses` then neither attaches to the review's own live or interrupted lens task nor copies any lens run, and `checkReusable` and `startAdjudication` reuse nothing either. So every pnpm install loses attachment for good, though the decision calls that layout identified. The only test of pnpm store links (`keeps a link between a pnpm store's packages inside`) reads from the install root, where the chain holds only the root, so it never sees this case.

properties.failureScenario: Take a pnpm checkout with `@stryker-mutator/instrumenter` installed. pnpm puts it at `node_modules/.pnpm/@stryker-mutator+instrumenter@X/node_modules/@stryker-mutator/instrumenter`, with `@babel/core` and its other dependencies as sibling links into `node_modules/.pnpm/@babel+core@7.x/node_modules/@babel/core`. A review offers a lens `list_mutants`, and `TypeScriptMutationAdapter.open` resolves the checkout's instrumenter. `install()` calls `Install.read(module)`, whose chain is [`.pnpm/@stryker-mutator+instrumenter@X`, checkout root]. Following `.pnpm/@stryker-mutator+instrumenter@X/node_modules/@babel/core` sets `project` to `chain[0]`. The target is not beneath it, so the walk records `links outside` and the install's `identified` is false. In `reviewChangeset`, `reusable` becomes false, and `runLenses` skips both the attach and `copiesFrom` for every lens, the ones not offered `list_mutants` included. A second `melian review` of the same head, or a rerun after a crash (the skills tell users a killed review resumes when run again), asks every lens again: about $5 a round here, every round, on every pnpm checkout. Melian installed with pnpm (`pnpm add -g`) has the same shape for its own install, since `code-version.js` sits under `.pnpm/@melian-agent+pipeline@X`. `melianInstall().identified` is then always false. No lens run, check run or adjudication is ever reused, and doctor wrongly reports a link outside Melian's install.
